claim: LARP4 directly binds both poly(A) and poly(A)-binding protein (PABP).
source: La-related protein 4 (LARP4) directly binds both poly(A) and poly(A)-binding protein (PABP).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work (Cruz-Gallardo et al., 2019; Yang et al., 2011) as stated in the manuscript.

claim: LARP4 was shown to promote poly(A) tail (PAT) lengthening and stabilization of individual mRNAs presumably by protection from deadenylation.
source: LARP4 was shown to promote poly(A) tail (PAT) lengthening and stabilization of individual mRNAs presumably by protection from deadenylation (Mattijssen et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Mattijssen et al., 2017.

claim: SM-PAT-seq is a nucleotide resolution transcriptome-wide, single molecule method developed by the authors.
source: We developed a nucleotide resolution transcriptome-wide, single molecule SM-PAT-seq method.
evidence: The manuscript describes the development and methodology of SM-PAT-seq in the Results section and Materials and methods.

claim: LARP4 effects on PAT lengths were revealed for a wide range of PAT lengths for human mRNAs and mouse mRNAs from LARP4 knockout (KO) and control cells.
source: This revealed LARP4 effects on a wide range of PAT lengths for human mRNAs and mouse mRNAs from LARP4 knockout (KO) and control cells.
evidence: This is supported by the SM-PAT-seq data presented in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: LARP4 effects are clear on long PAT mRNAs but become more prominent at 30–75 nucleotides.
source: LARP4 effects are clear on long PAT mRNAs but become more prominent at 30–75 nucleotides.
evidence: This is supported by the SM-PAT-seq data analysis shown in Figures 2, 3, and 5.

claim: Time course analysis demonstrated accelerated deadenylation in KO cells on PATs < 75 nucleotides.
source: This demonstrated accelerated deadenylation in KO cells on PATs < 75 nucleotides and phasing consistent with greater PABP dissociation in the absence of LARP4.
evidence: This is supported by the time course SM-PAT-seq data in Figure 5.

claim: LARP4 shapes PAT profiles throughout mRNA lifespan with impact on mRNA decay at short lengths known to sensitize PABP dissociation in response to deadenylation machinery.
source: Thus, LARP4 shapes PAT profiles throughout mRNA lifespan with impact on mRNA decay at short lengths known to sensitize PABP dissociation in response to deadenylation machinery.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the SM-PAT-seq data presented throughout the manuscript, particularly Figures 2, 3, and 5.

claim: PABP is a translation factor which by binding to eIF4G can link the mRNA 5' cap and associated initiation factors with translation termination factors and the 3' PAT.
source: PABP is a translation factor which by binding to eIF4G can link the mRNA 5' cap and associated initiation factors with translation termination factors and the 3' PAT (Uchida et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Uchida et al., 2002.

claim: Nascent precursor-mRNAs acquire PATs in the nucleus and enter the cytoplasm with lengths of ~250 nt that shorten thereafter with gene-specific multifaceted kinetics.
source: Nascent precursor-mRNAs acquire PATs in the nucleus and enter the cytoplasm with lengths of ~250 nt that shorten thereafter with gene-specific multifaceted kinetics (reviewed in Chen and Shyu, 2017; Jalkanen et al., 2014; Nicholson and Pasquinelli, 2019; Yamashita et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to review articles.

claim: Multiple PABP molecules can bind to poly(A) with a periodicity of ~27 nt.
source: Multiple PABP molecules can bind to poly(A) with a periodicity of ~27 nt (Baer and Kornberg, 1980; Nicholson and Pasquinelli, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Baer and Kornberg, 1980 and Nicholson and Pasquinelli, 2019.

claim: PABP architecture is conserved, consisting of four RNA recognition motifs (RRMs), followed by a helix, a flexible linker and a globular C-terminal Mademoiselle (MLLE) domain with a binding site for a PAM2 peptide.
source: PABP architecture is conserved, consisting of four RNA recognition motifs (RRMs), followed by a helix, a flexible linker (Schäfer et al., 2019) and a globular C-terminal Mademoiselle (MLLE) domain with a binding site for a PAM2 peptide.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Schäfer et al., 2019 and represents established knowledge about PABP structure.

claim: About 20 distinct proteins contain PAM2 peptides, of which several play key roles in mRNA metabolism and/or translation.
source: About 20 distinct proteins contain PAM2 peptides, of which several play key roles in mRNA metabolism and/or translation (Xie et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Xie et al., 2014.

claim: PATs became longer after PABP depletion in vivo.
source: While earlier experiments had shown PAT shortening after PABP depletion from cell extracts, PATs became longer after PABP depletion in vivo (Sachs and Davis, 1989).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Sachs and Davis, 1989.

claim: PABP promotes PAT shortening by recruiting the PAM2-containing proteins, PAN3, Tob1, Tob2, GW182 and their associated deadenylases.
source: PABP promotes PAT shortening by recruiting the PAM2-containing proteins, PAN3, Tob1, Tob2, GW182 and their associated deadenylases (reviewed in Xie et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a review by Xie et al., 2014.

claim: LARP4 is also known as LARP4A.
source: LARP4, which is also known as LARP4A directly binds poly(A) RNA and PABP (Cruz-Gallardo et al., 2019; Yang et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text.

claim: LARP4 is a short-lived protein whose accumulation levels can span a wide range due in part to control by independent instability elements located in the coding region and in the 3'UTR of its mRNA.
source: LARP4 is a short-lived protein whose accumulation levels can span a wide range due in part to control by independent instability elements located in the coding region and in the 3'UTR of its mRNA (Mattijssen et al., 2017; Mattijssen and Maraia, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Mattijssen et al., 2017 and Mattijssen and Maraia, 2016.

claim: LARP4 contains a La motif followed by a RNA recognition motif (RRM), and LARP-specific domains.
source: As with other La-related proteins (LARPs), LARP4 contains a La motif followed by a RNA recognition motif (RRM), and LARP-specific domains (Maraia et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Maraia et al., 2017.

claim: LARP4 binds PABP via two motifs, an N-terminal variant PAM2 named PAM2w and a downstream PABP-binding motif (PBM), both of which are required for efficient polysome association and stabilization of poly(A)+ mRNA.
source: LARP4 binds PABP via two motifs, an N-terminal variant PAM2 named PAM2w and a downstream PABP-binding motif (PBM), both of which are required for efficient polysome association and stabilization of poly(A)+ mRNA (Mattijssen et al., 2017; Yang et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Mattijssen et al., 2017 and Yang et al., 2011.

claim: LARP4 effects on PATs were documented as their apparent net-lengthening on reporter as well as endogenous mRNAs.
source: LARP4 effects on PATs were documented as their apparent net-lengthening on reporter as well as endogenous mRNAs.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Mattijssen et al., 2017 in the following sentence.

claim: The poly(A) on existing or newly synthesized mRNA is relatively protected from deadenylation in cells in which LARP4 is overexpressed.
source: This reflects that the poly(A) on existing or newly synthesized mRNA is relatively protected from deadenylation in cells in which LARP4 is overexpressed (Mattijssen et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Mattijssen et al., 2017.

claim: The PAT length of stable GFP mRNA bearing a short 3' UTR was dose-dependent on LARP4 levels.
source: The PAT length of stable GFP mRNA bearing a short 3' UTR was dose-dependent on LARP4 levels (Mattijssen et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Mattijssen et al., 2017.

claim: PAT lengthening and stabilization were observed for a β-globin reporter mRNA with an AU-rich element (ARE) that was previously known to be destabilized via recruitment of the CCR-NOT deadenylase complex.
source: PAT lengthening and stabilization were also observed for a β-globin reporter mRNA with an AU-rich element (ARE) that was previously known to be destabilized via recruitment of the CCR-NOT deadenylase complex (Fabian et al., 2013; Mattijssen et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Fabian et al., 2013 and Mattijssen et al., 2017.

claim: Endogenous mRNAs exhibited shorter PATs and decreased stability in LARP4 KO cells relative to LARP4 WT cells.
source: Endogenous mRNAs exhibited shorter PATs and decreased stability in LARP4 KO cells relative to LARP4 WT cells (Mattijssen et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Mattijssen et al., 2017.

claim: Full PAT net-lengthening and mRNA stabilization activity of LARP4 requires its PABP-interaction motifs albeit the PBM more so than the PAM2w.
source: Full PAT net-lengthening and mRNA stabilization activity of LARP4 requires its PABP-interaction motifs albeit the PBM more so than the PAM2w (Mattijssen et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Mattijssen et al., 2017.

claim: Each circularized DNA representing a single mRNA molecule with its full length PAT is replicated multiple times, both the sense strand and its complement.
source: Each circularized DNA representing a single mRNA molecule with its full length PAT is replicated multiple times, both the sense strand and its complement (Figure 1B).
evidence: This describes the SM-PAT-seq methodology as shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Multiple 'subreads' generate one circular consensus sequence (CCS) read containing a unique gene-derived mRNA fragment followed by a nucleotide length-resolved PAT specific to the single mRNA molecule it represents.
source: Multiple 'subreads' generate one circular consensus sequence (CCS) read containing a unique gene-derived mRNA fragment followed by a nucleotide length-resolved PAT specific to the single mRNA molecule it represents (Figure 1B).
evidence: This describes the SM-PAT-seq methodology as shown in Figure 1B.

claim: SM-PAT-seq and RNA-seq showed an R2 correlation = 0.58 with p value of 2.2e-16 when analyzing the same RNA sample.
source: The same RNA sample was analyzed for transcriptome-wide read counts by both methods and revealed an R2 correlation = 0.58 with p value of 2.2e-16 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by the comparative analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Triplicate quantifications of GFP mRNA by SM-PAT-Seq and northern blotting produced an R2 correlation = 0.96 with a p=0.000035.
source: Triplicate quantifications of GFP mRNA by SM-PAT-Seq and northern blotting produced an R2 correlation = 0.96 with a p=0.000035 (next section).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: >99% of SM-PAT-seq CCS reads reflect single molecule mRNAs as <1% CCS read identity was detected per library.
source: Finally, we note that >99% of SM-PAT-seq CCS reads reflect single molecule mRNAs as <1% CCS read identity was detected per library (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by the analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: SM-PAT-Seq was performed on HEK293 cells expressing LARP4 at three levels: ~1X (endogenous), ~3X, and ~11X.
source: Cells received empty plasmid or plasmid expressing LARP4 at ~3X or ~11X higher than endogenous LARP4 levels (1X) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), and each also received a uniform amount of GFP expression plasmid.
evidence: This is supported by the experimental design described in the text and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: SM-PAT-Seq analysis revealed effects on ~13,500 nuclear-encoded mRNAs in HEK293 cells.
source: Figure 2A shows effects on PAT lengths for ~13,500 nuclear-encoded mRNAs (includes poly(A)+ transcripts annotated as long noncoding RNAs) (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 2A and Supplementary file 1.

claim: LARP4 expression led to shifts in mRNA PAT length distributions in three length ranges: 30–60 nt, 60–90 nt, and 90- > 250 nt.
source: LARP4 expression led to shifts in mRNA PAT length distributions in three length ranges (Figure 2A), 30–60 nt, 60–90 nt, and 90- > 250 nt.
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: At 11X LARP4, the fraction most increased was mRNAs with long PATs, 150–250 nt.
source: At 11X, the fraction most increased was mRNAs with long PATs, 150–250 nt.
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The intersection of the 1X and 11X tracings was at 110–90 nt.
source: The intersection of the 1X and 11X tracings was at 110–90 nt.
evidence: This is observed in the data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The median PAT length 50% cumulative read fraction was shifted from ~75 nt with 1X LARP4 to ~82 and~90 nt at 3X and 11X LARP4, respectively.
source: The median PAT length 50% cumulative read fraction was shifted from ~75 nt with 1X LARP4 to ~82 and~90 nt at 3X and 11X LARP4, respectively (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The average PAT lengths for functionally related gene subsets as determined by gene ontology (GO) were almost all correlated with LARP4 expression levels, with the one clear exception being the mitochondrial DNA-encoded mRNAs.
source: The average PAT lengths for functionally related gene subsets as determined by gene ontology (GO) were almost all correlated with LARP4 expression levels, with the one clear exception being the mitochondrial DNA-encoded mRNAs, as expected (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The nuclear-encoded mitochondrion mRNAs had PATs significantly shorter than most other mRNAs in cells with 1X LARP4, and their lengths increased less in response to higher LARP4 levels.
source: However, an unexpected exception was the set of nuclear-encoded mitochondrion mRNAs. The PATs on the mRNAs that comprise this set are significantly shorter than on most other mRNAs in cells with 1X LARP4, and their lengths increased less in response to higher LARP4 levels relative to the PAT length increases in the other mRNA GO sets.
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: GFP mRNA accumulation and PAT lengthening was dose-dependent on LARP4.
source: This showed that GFP mRNA accumulation and PAT lengthening was dose-dependent on LARP4 (Figure 2E,F).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figures 2E and 2F.

claim: As LARP4 levels increased, GFP mRNA median PAT lengths increased and were accompanied by increases in GFP CCS reads.
source: As LARP4 levels increased, GFP mRNA median PAT lengths increased and were accompanied by increases in GFP CCS reads (Figure 2F), reflective of the trends of GFP mRNA levels and mobility shifts seen by northern blot (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figures 2E and 2F.

claim: Comparison of GFP CCS quantitative reads and GFP mRNA quantitation by northern revealed a R2 value of 0.96 with p=0.000035.
source: Comparison of GFP CCS quantitative reads and GFP mRNA quantitation by northern revealed a R2 value of 0.96 with p=0.000035 (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: SM-PAT-Seq analysis of ~10,500 nuclear-encoded mRNA CCS reads from triplicate MEF cell lines showed that KO MEFs have more mRNA CCS reads with short PATs (30–60 nt) than with longer PATs (75–200 nt) as compared to WT.
source: The left panel of Figure 3A shows SM-PAT-Seq analysis of ~10,500 nuclear-encoded mRNA CCS reads from triplicate MEF cell lines (Supplementary file 2). The KO MEFs have more mRNA CCS reads with short PATs (30–60 nt) than with longer PATs (75–200 nt) as compared to WT (Figure 3A, left panel).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The median PAT lengths of KO MEF mRNAs are shorter than in WT MEFs, for thousands of mRNAs.
source: Violin plots (Figure 3B) show that the median PAT lengths of KO MEF mRNAs are shorter than in WT MEFs, for thousands of mRNAs.
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: LARP4 expression had no apparent effect on mitochondrial DNA-encoded mRNA PATs.
source: In contrast to nuclear DNA gene-encoded mRNAs, LARP4 expression had no apparent effect on mitochondrial DNA-encoded mRNA PATs (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Occurrence of sequential peaks in the poly(A) length profiles of efficiently translated mRNAs such as those that encode ribosomal proteins is referred to as phasing.
source: Occurrence of sequential peaks in the poly(A) length profiles of efficiently translated mRNAs such as those that encode ribosomal proteins is referred to as phasing (Lima et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Lima et al., 2017.

claim: The phased PAT length peaks derive from fluctuations in the rates of deadenylation around sites protected by serial PABPs bound at those positions.
source: The phased PAT length peaks derive from fluctuations in the rates of deadenylation around sites protected by serial PABPs bound at those positions (Lima et al., 2017; Nicholson and Pasquinelli, 2019) (see Yi et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Lima et al., 2017, Nicholson and Pasquinelli, 2019, and Yi et al., 2018.

claim: Three ribosomal protein (rp) mRNAs have shorter PATs and shorter half-lives in LARP4 KO MEF cell lines as compared to WT MEF cell lines.
source: It was previously shown that three ribosomal protein (rp) mRNAs have shorter PATs and shorter half-lives in LARP4 KO MEF cell lines as compared to WT MEF cell lines (Mattijssen et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Mattijssen et al., 2017.

claim: Both WT and KO rp-mRNA profiles revealed a bimodal distribution in the ~35–70 nt size range, although the relative heights of the two peaks clearly differed in WT and KO.
source: The left panel shows that both profiles revealed a bimodal distribution in the ~35–70 nt size range, although the relative heights of the two peaks clearly differed in WT and KO.
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Genetic deletion of LARP4 alters the PAT length phasing pattern of rp-mRNAs in MEFs in the ~70–35 nt size range.
source: We conclude that genetic deletion of LARP4 alters the PAT length phasing pattern of rp-mRNAs in MEFs in the ~70–35 nt size range, and this is associated with differences in profile shapes of longer PATs.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: An ARE in LARP4 mRNA mediates decreased LARP4 levels in response to the cytokine tumor necrosis factor-α (TNFα).
source: An ARE in LARP4 mRNA mediates decreased LARP4 levels in response to the cytokine tumor necrosis factor-α (TNFα) (Mattijssen and Maraia, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Mattijssen and Maraia, 2016.

claim: Triplicate RNA-seq revealed that a set of 128 ISG mRNAs were induced to ≥1.5 fold higher levels with a Padj-value <0.05 in HEK293 cells expressing 3X LARP4 relative to 1X after 1 kb AT-rich DNA transfection.
source: Triplicate RNA-seq revealed that a set of 128 ISG mRNAs were induced to ≥1.5 fold higher levels with a Padj-value <0.05 in HEK293 cells expressing 3X LARP4 relative to 1X after 1 kb AT-rich DNA transfection (Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is supported by the RNA-seq data in Supplementary file 3.

claim: Higher levels of ISG mRNAs accumulated with elevated LARP4 (+) expression after poly(I:C) transfection.
source: This verified that higher levels of ISG mRNAs accumulated with elevated LARP4 (+) expression (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 4A and 4B.

claim: Slower mobility was observed in the ISG15 mRNA from the cells transfected with LARP4 (+), indicative of longer PATs.
source: Slower mobility was observed in the ISG15 mRNA from the cells transfected with LARP4 (+), indicative of longer PATs (Figure 4A, lanes 2 and 4, 6 and 8, 10 and 12).
evidence: This is supported by the northern blot data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Cells expressing 3X higher levels of LARP4 produced more ISG mRNA at a lower dose of inducing DNA.
source: The cells expressing 3X higher levels of LARP4 produced more ISG mRNA at a lower dose of inducing DNA.
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: LARP4 expression can contribute to the levels to which ISG mRNAs accumulate after their induction.
source: Thus LARP4 expression can contribute to the levels to which ISG mRNAs accumulate after their induction (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Increased accumulation of IFIT1 and ISG15 mRNAs is dependent on the PABP-interaction motifs PAM2w and PBM, of LARP4.
source: Examination of different LARP4 constructs revealed that increased accumulation of IFIT1 and ISG15 mRNAs is dependent on the PABP-interaction motifs PAM2w and PBM, of LARP4, also required for GFP mRNA mobility shift indicative of PAT protection (Figure 4D; Mattijssen et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 4D and citation to Mattijssen et al., 2017.

claim: ISG15 mRNA has a ~ 4 hr half-life in WT cells, consistent with prior data, but 2.8 hr in KO cells, reflecting lower stability.
source: As part of the same duplicate experiments, northern blots of total RNA revealed a ~ 4 hr half-life for ISG15 mRNA in WT cells, consistent with prior data (Li et al., 2000), but 2.8 hr in KO cells, reflecting lower stability (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: This is supported by the northern blot data shown in Figures 5A and 5B, and citation to Li et al., 2000.

claim: The ISG15 mRNA bands exhibited progressively faster mobility with time after ActD reflective of deadenylation.
source: The ISG15 mRNA bands exhibited progressively faster mobility with time after ActD reflective of deadenylation (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by the northern blot data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: At 30 min after ActD, a significant fraction of mRNAs appeared with shorter PATs, with a peak at 35–40 nt in the KO profile, while no such peak fraction was distinguished in the WT profile.
source: A more striking feature was observed at 30 min as a significant fraction of mRNAs appeared with shorter PATs, with a peak at 35–40 nt in the KO profile, while no such peak fraction was distinguished in the WT profile (Figure 5C, panel t = 30).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: By 60 min the WT profile showed a fraction of mRNA PATs of ~35–40 nt similar to what appeared earlier in the KO profile.
source: By 60 min the WT profile showed a fraction of mRNA PATs of ~35–40 nt similar to what appeared earlier in the KO profile.
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The t = 0 peak at ~75 nt shrank with time as the 35–40 nt peak enlarged, as expected of a precursor-product relationship.
source: A substantial amount of the total mRNA mass shifted to shorter PATs during the time course. The t = 0 peak at ~75 nt shrank with time as the 35–40 nt peak enlarged, as expected of a precursor-product relationship (compare t = 60, 120, 240, 480).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: By the t = 720 min time, a single ~38 nt peak is in the KO profile while the WT profile retains remnants of the precursor ~75 nt peak.
source: By the t = 720 min time, a single ~38 nt peak is in the KO profile while the WT profile retains remnants of the precursor ~75 nt peak.
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Conversion of the distinct mass of the ~75 nt PAT peak to ~38 nt PATs was initiated faster and completed more readily in LARP4 KO than in WT cells.
source: Thus, conversion of the distinct mass of the ~75 nt PAT peak to ~38 nt PATs was initiated faster and completed more readily in LARP4 KO than in WT cells.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The presence of LARP4 slows deadenylation and this becomes most apparent at the point beyond which mRNAs accumulate with poly(A) lengths of ~75 nt.
source: The time course PAT decay data in Figure 5C provide evidence that the presence of LARP4 slows deadenylation and this becomes most apparent at the point beyond which mRNAs accumulate with poly(A) lengths of ~75 nt.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: A set of 194 ISG mRNAs was identified by inducing them in MEFs.
source: We identified a set of 194 ISG mRNAs by inducing them in MEFs (Supplementary file 4) and examined their PAT shortening at times after ActD.
evidence: This is supported by the data in Supplementary file 4.

claim: The greatest variability in PAT length sorted with the longest PATs, consistent with recent observations.
source: By this approach, the greatest variability in PAT length sorted with the longest PATs, consistent with recent observations (Eisen et al., 2020b).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C and citation to Eisen et al., 2020b.

claim: At t = 0 the ISG peak at 35–40 nt for the KO tracing is slightly to the left and higher on the Y-axis than the WT peak, suggesting relative accelerated PAT shortening in the KO cells during the IFN treatment period.
source: At t = 0 the ISG peak at 35–40 nt for the KO tracing is slightly to the left and higher on the Y-axis than the WT peak, which is below the 0.010 fraction level, suggesting relative accelerated PAT shortening in the KO cells during the IFN treatment period (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Shortening of mRNA PATs to ones that accumulate with ~38 nt PATs occurred more readily in LARP4 KO than in WT cells.
source: They showed that shortening of mRNA PATs to ones that accumulate with ~38 nt PATs occurred more readily in LARP4 KO than in WT cells.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: By following mRNA PAT lengths over time, deadenylation was observed to occur with less impediment in the absence of LARP4 than in its presence.
source: Thus, by following mRNA PAT lengths over time, deadenylation was observed to occur with less impediment in the absence of LARP4 than in its presence.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the time course data shown in Figure 5.

claim: LARP4 is a general factor that slows deadenylation transcriptome-wide, impacting a large fraction of mRNAs.
source: A major conclusion is that LARP4 is a general factor that slows deadenylation transcriptome-wide, impacting a large fraction of mRNAs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the SM-PAT-seq data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: For HEK293 cells and MEFs, LARP4 protects PATs from deadenylation over a wide spectrum of lengths, long and short.
source: For HEK293 cells and MEFs, LARP4 protects PATs from deadenylation over a wide spectrum of lengths, long and short.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the SM-PAT-seq data presented in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: mRNAs are deadenylated faster in KO than in WT cells.
source: By examining PAT length after inhibition of transcription we conclude that mRNAs are deadenylated faster in KO than in WT cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the time course data shown in Figure 5.

claim: PATs of ≤75 nt are more susceptible to deadenylation in the absence of LARP4 than in its presence.
source: The data indicate that PATs of ≤75 nt are more susceptible to deadenylation in the absence of LARP4 than in its presence.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the SM-PAT-seq data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: LARP4 slows conversion of long PAT- to short PAT-mRNAs.
source: Data in Figures 2A and 3A–C provide evidence that LARP4 slows conversion of long PAT- to short PAT-mRNAs.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data shown in Figures 2A and 3A-C.

claim: The PATs of the stable GFP mRNA expressed in transiently transfected HEK293 were longer than the cellular mRNAs likely reflecting that they are newly transcribed whereas the latter comprise a steady state population of mixed species.
source: The PATs of the stable GFP mRNA expressed in transiently transfected HEK293 were longer than the cellular mRNAs (Figure 2B,F) likely reflecting that they are newly transcribed whereas the latter comprise a steady state population of mixed species (Eisen et al., 2020b).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data shown in Figures 2B and 2F, with citation to Eisen et al., 2020b.

claim: LARP4 can increase the stability of stable GFP mRNA by protecting against deadenylation during its lifespan when PATs are long.
source: Thus, it would appear that LARP4 can increase the stability of this stable GFP mRNA by protecting against deadenylation during its lifespan when PATs are long.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data shown in Figures 2E and 2F.

claim: LARP4 can stabilize both stable mRNA and unstable mRNA.
source: LARP4 can stabilize both stable mRNA and unstable mRNA (Mattijssen et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Mattijssen et al., 2017.

claim: A change in LARP4 levels at a single time point can differentially affect turnover of different sets of mRNAs at different times thereafter, depending on characteristics of their lifespan poly(A) profiles.
source: Thus, it is possible that a change in LARP4 levels at a single time point can differentially affect turnover of different sets of mRNAs at different times thereafter, depending on characteristics of their lifespan poly(A) profiles.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the data presented.

claim: Pan2-Pan3 can efficiently trim long PATs with serially bound PABP in part because of a unique architecture of PABP-PABP interactions on poly(A), whereas Pan2-Pan3 is inefficient on short poly(A)-PABP mRNPs.
source: Biochemical and structural studies of yeast factors indicate that Pan2-Pan3 can efficiently trim long PATs with serially bound PABP in part because of a unique architecture of PABP-PABP interactions on poly(A), whereas Pan2-Pan3 is inefficient on short poly(A)-PABP mRNPs (Schäfer et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Schäfer et al., 2019.

claim: PABP recruits the CNOT complex to promote deadenylation of shorter PATs, but the CCR4 and CAF1 deadenylase subunits respond very differently.
source: Biochemical studies using human factors showed that although PABP recruits the CNOT complex to promote deadenylation of shorter PATs, the CCR4 and CAF1 deadenylase subunits respond very differently (Yi et al., 2018), consistent with studies using the yeast homologs (Schäfer et al., 2019; Webster et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Yi et al., 2018, Schäfer et al., 2019, and Webster et al., 2018.

claim: The Ccr4 subunit is required to dislodge or peel off PABP.
source: The Caf1 subunit of CNOT can deadenylate unprotected poly(A) but the Ccr4 subunit is required to dislodge or peel off PABP (Webster et al., 2018; Yi et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Webster et al., 2018 and Yi et al., 2018.

claim: PAT length phasing is more sharply prominent in human cell lines whose CCR4 levels were decreased.
source: PAT length phasing is related to nonuniform deadenylation around PABP sites and was shown to be more sharply prominent in human cell lines whose CCR4 levels were decreased (Yi et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Yi et al., 2018.

claim: Deadenylation progressively accelerates as bound PABP decreases to two then to one molecule and thereafter.
source: The biochemistry indicates that deadenylation progressively accelerates as bound PABP decreases to two then to one molecule and thereafter (Webster et al., 2018; Yi et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Webster et al., 2018 and Yi et al., 2018.
